deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page is a working draft of the opening of Riemann's natural-philosophy fragment on gravitation and light. The published Werke fragment 'Gravitation und Licht' begins in essentially the same way. The next page continues with the aether-flow hypothesis. The page derives nothing new. It axiomatizes Newtonian point mechanics so that the gravitational field can later be identified with the velocity field of a space-filling 'Stoff'.

Top lines (end of the previous draft passage). The change of state with which the Stoff disappears from the corporeal world determines the new state of the 'Geistesmasse' (mind-mass) formed from it. This is Riemann's known speculative idea that matter absorbs aether, which passes into a mental realm.

Main text: 'To explain the laws of fall and the motions of the heavenly bodies, the following hypotheses have served since Newton, besides the geometric axioms.'

(1) Inertia. A ponderable point that is alone in space either stays at rest or moves with constant velocity on a straight line: x(t) = x0 + v0 t, so that d^2x/dt^2 = 0. Riemann's philosophical remark: this law of persistence cannot be derived from the concept of a ponderable point by the principle of sufficient reason. That the point continues its motion must have a cause, which can lie only in its state.

(2) Every deviation from uniform rectilinear motion is the consequence of a change of the point's state, for which a cause must be sought.

(3) Every change of motion can be regarded as a motion that composes geometrically, by the parallelogram rule, with the motion already present. In modern terms, velocity v(t+dt) = v(t) + dv, with vector addition. Hence the causes of changes of motion must be distinguished by magnitude and direction: they are vectors.

(4) At every place and instant there exists a definite force F(x,t), i.e. a cause determined in magnitude and direction. It would change the motion of a ponderable point located there according to two rules.
- (i) The same ponderable point would undergo, at two places, accelerations a parallel to the forces there, with |a1|:|a2| = |F1|:|F2|.
- (ii) Hence F/a is the same constant for a given point. It differs between points and is called the point's mass: F = m a.

Second item (4), also numbered 4; the numbering is duplicated. The accelerating force at a given place and instant depends on the configuration of all ponderable points. If one ponderable point were alone, at every point of space there would be a force directed toward it, with magnitude proportional to 1/r^2: g(x) = -M (x - x0)/|x - x0|^3. The product |g| r^2 is therefore the same for all points of space and is called the point's mass M. This is the active gravitational mass, with units chosen so that G = 1.

Right-hand marginal draft. A variant of hypothesis 3/4: at each point of space and instant there exists a cause, determined in magnitude and direction, which would change the motion of a ponderable point placed there.

Next page (my summary). It adds superposition of the fields of the individual points. It then posits a continuous Stoff whose velocity is parallel to the force and proportional to its magnitude. For a single point source the radial inflow v ~ 1/r^2 has div v = 0 for r != 0, so the same quantity of Stoff always occupies the same volume (incompressible flow). Matter must therefore swallow Stoff at a rate proportional to its attracting mass. This is my modern reading of 'dieselbe Menge des Stoffes stets denselben Raum einnimmt' and is certain.
errors: Terminological inconsistency, not a mathematical error. In the first item 4, 'Kraft' at a place is treated as a field that would act on any point, yet the quotient Kraft/Bewegungsänderung is said to give the point's mass. That requires 'Kraft' to mean motive force on the body. If it meant the place-dependent field, the quotient would be the same for all bodies, as in the equivalence principle.

In the second item 4, 'beschleunigende Kraft' (accelerating force, i.e. acceleration field) is used, and F*r^2 defines the source's mass. Two different notions of mass are thus defined with the same word, inertial m = F/a and active gravitational M = g r^2, without stating their equality or the constant G.
Item number 4 appears twice (draft state). The phrase 'Bewegungsänderung' leaves open whether acceleration or velocity increment over a fixed time is meant; this is harmless.
The claim that inertia 'cannot be explained from the principle of sufficient reason' is a philosophical assertion, not a derivation.

results.what: Axiomatic restatement of Newton's laws for ponderable points: inertia, parallelogram composition of changes of motion, F = m a with mass defined as the constant ratio force/acceleration
results.modern_name: Newton's laws of motion; operational (Machian-type) definition of inertial mass
results.usually_credited_to: Newton (1687); the ratio definition of mass is often associated with Mach (1868/1883)

results.what: Field of a single ponderable point: directed toward it, proportional to 1/r^2, with g r^2 = const defining the source mass
results.modern_name: Newtonian inverse-square gravitational field; active gravitational mass

results.what: Preparation for the gravitational field as the velocity field of an incompressible space-filling aether flowing into matter (completed on the next page)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann ('Gravitation und Licht', Werke 1876); similar ideas in Euler and later Bjerknes

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of material printed in Riemann's Werke (natural-philosophy fragments, 'Gravitation und Licht'). The content is a standard axiomatization of Newtonian mechanics and the inverse-square law. The only mildly interesting detail is the operational definition of mass as the constant ratio force/acceleration, which predates Mach's 1868 formulation. Even this is known from the published fragments and is not sharply formulated here.

checkable.sympy: x,y,z,M=symbols('x y z M',positive=True); r=sqrt(x**2+y**2+z**2); g=[-M*x/r**3,-M*y/r**3,-M*z/r**3]; simplify(diff(g[0],x)+diff(g[1],y)+diff(g[2],z))
checkable.asserts: The inverse-square field directed toward a point is divergence-free away from the source (result 0). This underlies the incompressibility claim on the next page.
The magnitude of the force times the square of the distance is the same constant M at all points of space (result 0).
Uniform rectilinear motion has zero acceleration (hypothesis 1, result 0).
If F = m a with fixed m, forces at two places are in the same ratio as the accelerations (item 4, rule i; result 0).

transcription_corrections: Line 3: 'ehe gebildeten Geisteskraft' most likely reads 'der aus ihm (ihr) gebildeten Geistesmasse'. Riemann's term 'Geistesmasse' fits the context of Stoff vanishing from the corporeal world.
Line 2: the word read as 'Zustandsänderung' is uncertain in the image (possibly '...form'). The cancelled phrase is 'mit welcher der verschwindende Stoff'.

Hypothesis 1: the struck-through 'Körper' is replaced by the interlinear 'ponderable Punkt'. The surviving text reads 'Jeder ponderable Punkt würde, wenn er sich im Raume allein befände, ... nicht verändern oder mit unveränderlicher Geschwindigkeit in gerader Linie durch denselben sich bewegen' (the transcription marks too much as cancelled).

'aus dem Begriff des ponderablen Punkts aus zureichenden Gründen erklärt werden': the interlinear 'ponderablen Punkts' replaces a cancelled word. The transcription runs 'Begriff des' and 'zureichenden Gründen' together incorrectly.

Item 4 (first) ends 'nach folgendem Gesetz verändern würde.' Sub-item 1: 'Derselbe ponderable Punkt würde an zwei verschiedenen Orten Bewegungsänderungen erleiden, deren Richtung mit der Richtung der Kräfte zusammenfällt und deren Größe sich verhält wie die Kräfte'.

Second item 4 opening: 'Die beschleunigende Kraft, die in einem bestimmten Orte in jedem Augenblicke stattfindet, hängt in jedem Augenblicke ab von der Anordnung aller ponderablen Punkte'. Here 'hängt' is probably not cancelled.

Right margin, item 3: 'In jedem Punkte des Raumes existirt in jedem Augenblicke eine nach Größe und Richtung bestimmte Ursache, welche die Bewegung eines dort befindlichen ponderablen Punktes verändern würde'.
